fact: Smart Zambia announced plans for an e-Council system to digitise revenue management and financial reporting in all local authorities, letting councils identify revenue streams and track collections in real time; no register of payers is described.

Phase one is a proof of concept in eight councils (Ndola, Kalulushi, Kalumbila, Kitwe, Solwezi, Chingola, Chilanga and one more), with system demonstration expected by 19 June 2026, before extension to the rest.
The e-Council is announced by Smart Zambia, the state digital agency, as part of the national e-government plan.
Government chief technical officer says all 116 local authorities are connected to the government network and have solar power, groundwork for the e-Council rollout planned for 2026.

The IGC policy brief states that in Zambia the prevailing use of manual systems and hard copy maps for administering property undermines councils' property tax revenue, and that most local councils still run on manual systems, with the few partly digitalised working in silos at department or section level; the date is the brief's own (May 2024).
system: manual property rate administration (paper records, ledgers, receipt books)

fact: The brief names councils' weak capacity to administer property tax, partly from outdated cadastres and poor record keeping, with many tax maps covering only a fraction of rateable properties; date is the brief's own (May 2024).
system: council property tax maps and valuation rolls
